objective: Integrate the accepted core, HTTP, WebSocket, oracle, and actor components into one runnable bounded service; add black-box acceptance probes, packaging, deployment assets, and operator/user documentation for a clearly labeled public synthetic demo.

assertions: A fresh checkout builds one runnable service, its liveness and readiness are distinguishable, and graceful shutdown terminates listeners, actors, oracle work, and the engine owner.
The black-box probe obtains metadata/mids/book data, subscribes to quotes and trades, creates a local order, observes its user update, and cancels an open order using X-Sim-User.
A stale-oracle probe shows placement rejection after greater than 60 seconds while cancellation remains available, and a safety probe observes no upstream state-changing requests.
The container/deployment applies bounded request bodies, order batches, command queues, WebSocket connections/buffers, and public rate limits without changing the frozen compatibility profile.

Deployment, operations, quickstart, and README material clearly label synthetic state and document sim-header-v1, fixed assets, seed/configuration, health, oracle fallback, unsupported behavior, and no-real-funds/no-upstream-trading boundaries.

deliverables: sim-server executable composition and validated configuration
Container and deployment/service assets for the public demo
Deployment, operations, quickstart, and top-level user documentation
risks: Public endpoint abuse can exhaust connections, queues, or memory.
TLS, firewall, process supervision, or upstream availability can make a local success non-reproducible externally.
Integration pressure can silently broaden compatibility or bypass accepted module interfaces.
notes: Shared manifest edits are unavoidable during final composition; product module directories remain forbidden so integration failures are repaired in their owning tasks rather than patched around here.
